questions.title: Check if String is Palindrome (Ignoring Case)
questions.problem_statement: Write an efficient function to check whether a given string is a palindrome, ignoring uppercase/lowercase differences and non-alphanumeric characters.
questions.hint: Use two pointers (one starting at index 0 and one at length-1) moving towards the center.

questions.title: Find Second Largest Element in an Array
questions.problem_statement: Given an integer array, find the second largest element in a single pass without sorting the array. Handle edge cases like duplicates or arrays with fewer than two unique elements.
questions.hint: Maintain two tracking variables: max1 and max2. Update max2 whenever a number is strictly between max1 and max2.

questions.title: Java Abstract Class vs Interface Differences
questions.problem_statement: Explain the key differences between an abstract class and an interface in Java (including default methods introduced in Java 8 and private methods in Java 9). When should you choose one over the other?
questions.hint: Focus on multiple inheritance of type vs implementation, field modifiers (final static), and design contract intent.

questions.title: Four Pillars of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
questions.problem_statement: Define Encapsulation, Abstraction, Inheritance, and Polymorphism. Give a practical real-world software example illustrating Method Overriding vs Method Overloading.
questions.hint: Overloading is compile-time (same method name, different parameters); Overriding is runtime (subclass redefines superclass method).

questions.title: SQL INNER JOIN vs LEFT JOIN Query
questions.problem_statement: Given two tables, Employees (emp_id, emp_name, dept_id) and Departments (dept_id, dept_name), write a query to fetch all employee names along with their department names, including employees who are not currently assigned to any department.
questions.hint: Use LEFT JOIN on Employees and Departments using dept_id.

questions.title: DBMS Primary Key vs Unique Key vs Foreign Key
questions.problem_statement: Explain the difference between Primary Key, Unique Key, and Foreign Key constraints in relational databases. Can a table have multiple Unique keys and multiple Foreign keys?
questions.hint: A table has exactly 1 Primary Key (no NULLs allowed). Unique keys permit one NULL value. Multiple Foreign keys can reference different parent tables.

questions.title: Operating Systems Process vs Thread & Multithreading Basics
questions.problem_statement: What is the difference between a Process and a Thread? Explain memory sharing between threads of the same process and why context switching between threads is faster than between processes.
questions.hint: Threads share text, data, and heap memory spaces, but maintain independent stacks and register sets.

questions.title: Computer Networks OSI Model Layers & HTTP vs HTTPS
questions.problem_statement: List the 7 layers of the OSI model. Explain how HTTP differs from HTTPS and which port numbers are used by default for both protocols.
questions.hint: HTTPS adds SSL/TLS encryption over port 443; HTTP operates unencrypted over port 80.

questions.title: Percentage Increase & Salary Calculation
questions.problem_statement: An employee's salary is increased by 20% in the first year and then decreased by 10% in the second year. If the current salary is $54,000, what was the initial salary before any changes?
questions.hint: Let initial salary be S. S * 1.20 * 0.90 = 54000 => S * 1.08 = 54000.

questions.title: Ratios & Team Allocation
questions.problem_statement: The ratio of male to female developers in a project team is 5:3. If there are 16 more male developers than female developers, what is the total number of developers in the team?
questions.hint: Let male = 5x and female = 3x. Difference = 2x = 16 => x = 8. Total = 8x = 64.

questions.title: Simple Interest vs Compound Interest
questions.problem_statement: The difference between simple interest and compound interest (compounded annually) on a principal amount at 10% per annum for 2 years is $45. What is the principal amount?
questions.hint: Formula for 2-year difference: Difference = P * (R/100)^2 => 45 = P * (10/100)^2.

questions.title: Time, Speed & Distance Train Problem
questions.problem_statement: A train 150 meters long is traveling at a constant speed of 54 km/h. How many seconds will it take to cross a standing platform 200 meters long?
questions.hint: Total distance = 150 + 200 = 350m. Speed in m/s = 54 * (5/18) = 15 m/s. Time = 350 / 15.

questions.title: Logical Reasoning Letter Series Coding
questions.problem_statement: In a certain code language, 'JAVA' is written as 'LCXC'. How is 'CODE' written in that same code language?
questions.hint: Pattern: Each letter is shifted forward by +2 positions in alphabetical order (J+2=L, A+2=C, V+2=X, A+2=C).

questions.title: Tell Me About Yourself
questions.problem_statement: Tell me about yourself, your educational background, key technical skills, and software projects.
questions.hint: Structure as Elevator Pitch: Current status/degree, technical competencies, major project highlight, and professional aspiration.

questions.title: Why Capgemini
questions.problem_statement: Why do you want to join Capgemini specifically?
questions.hint: Mention Capgemini's global presence, enterprise IT solutions, continuous learning culture, and digital transformation initiatives.

questions.title: Why Should We Hire You
questions.problem_statement: Why should Capgemini hire you over other candidates?
questions.hint: Align your strong programming foundation, fast learning ability, adaptability, and positive work ethic with Capgemini's goals.

questions.title: Strengths and Weaknesses
questions.problem_statement: What are your core technical/personal strengths and an area of weakness you are working to improve?
questions.hint: Pair a strong technical/analytical strength with a genuine weakness along with concrete steps you are taking to overcome it.

questions.title: Willingness to Relocate & Work Shifts
questions.problem_statement: Are you willing to relocate to different project locations and work in flexible project shifts if required by Capgemini?
questions.hint: Express flexibility, enthusiasm for new learning environments, and commitment to project success.

questions.title: Challenging Situation & Problem Resolution
questions.problem_statement: Describe a challenging situation during your academic or project journey and how you successfully handled it.
questions.hint: Use the STAR approach. Focus on problem breakdown, resourcefulness, composure, and positive resolution.
